evals.prompt: Our Dune app does not have COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN set. Use TyGen to generate client helpers for the EquipmentModel.
evals.expected_output: Do not apply TyGen or enable the flag. Explain that TyGen is an opt-in alpha capability and continue with the native @cognite/sdk APIs and types already used by the app.

assertions.text: Response requires COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN to be explicitly true before TyGen is used.
Response does not add or enable the alpha flag.
Response recommends the native @cognite/sdk as the fallback.

evals.prompt: COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN=true is already set for this app. Generate types for the data model production:EquipmentModel:v3 using the default output location.
evals.expected_output: Run cognite tygen generate with the versioned --data-model value and explain that the default output directory is src/generated_types/EquipmentModel/. The explicit generation request is sufficient confirmation.

assertions.text: Response uses cognite tygen generate rather than apps sdk types.
Response accepts the explicit generation request as confirmation and does not ask for redundant permission.
Response passes --data-model production:EquipmentModel:v3.
Response identifies src/generated_types/EquipmentModel as the default output directory.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is enabled and types are generated for PlantModel in src/generated_types/PlantModel. Show how to list the names of active Equipment in a React component.
evals.expected_output: Import initTygen from the generated index.ts, bind it to the client from useCogniteSdk(), and call tygen.equipment.query (or search) with a short-name filter on status and select ['name']. Read item.properties.name directly, without space and View/version nesting.

assertions.text: Response imports initTygen from the generated directory, not from @cognite/sdk.
Response calls a per-view method such as tygen.equipment.query or tygen.equipment.search.
The filter uses the short property name 'status', not a full [space, 'View/version', 'status'] path.
Response reads item.properties.name directly, without properties[space]['Equipment/1'] nesting.

evals.prompt: We changed a CDF data model after TyGen generation. Should I edit src/generated_types/EquipmentModel/types.ts to add the new field?
evals.expected_output: Regenerate from the versioned data model, inspect the generated diff, run typecheck and relevant tests, and commit the generated output with the app source. Do not hand-edit generated files.

assertions.text: Response instructs regeneration instead of hand-editing generated files.
Response requires inspecting the generated diff.
Response requires typecheck and relevant tests.
Response says to commit the generated output with the app source.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is enabled. I want to generate types but do not know the data model reference. I can use an interactive terminal and browser login. How should I run TyGen?
evals.expected_output: Run tygen generate without --data-model in an interactive terminal so the model picker selects a versioned model. Use --interactive for browser authentication and explain that it is independent of the model picker.

assertions.text: Response omits --data-model to use the interactive model picker.
Response uses --interactive for browser authentication and distinguishes it from the model picker.

evals.prompt: TyGen alpha is enabled. For each WorkOrder, show its name and the name of its mainAsset, which is a direct relation to FunctionalLocation in the same model.
evals.expected_output: Use tygen.workOrder.query with select ['name'] and include { mainAsset: { select: ['name'] } }, and read item.related.mainAsset?.properties?.name. No second request per work order.

assertions.text: Response uses include with the mainAsset relation in one tygen.workOrder.query call.
Response reads the related name from item.related.mainAsset, handling undefined.
Response does not fetch each related instance in a separate request.

evals.prompt: TyGen alpha is enabled. The work order list has optional filters for type and location. Build the filter from whichever are set and pass it to tygen.workOrder.query.
evals.expected_output: Spread in the conditions that are set, each ending in as const, and pass { and: conditions }. An empty and is fine.

assertions.text: Response spreads in the conditions that are set and ends each one in as const.
Response explains that without as const the property names widen to string and the call fails to typecheck.
Response does not cast the request to any or unknown.

evals.prompt: TyGen alpha is enabled. Count WorkOrders by workOrderType, which is an enum property, with tygen.workOrder.aggregate.
evals.expected_output: Explain that the API cannot group by an enum property, so groupBy rejects it. Count each enum value with its own aggregate: a count with an equals filter on that value.

assertions.text: Response says enum properties cannot be used in groupBy.
Response counts each enum value with a filtered count, one aggregate per value.
Response does not cast groupBy to bypass the type error.
